### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **90** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**44** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 76cb36661da9dba890c83e2130ff624f1ed29e90`.

⛔ **15** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `objectName (symbol, 59 pages)`, `master_detail (literal, 47 pages)`
- **19** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **67** of **249** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 76cb36661da9dba890c83e2130ff624f1ed29e90` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1140eed193f9f1e2669f0c3193134eb76d3c8a95` — the merge of head `42d56e66cbcb04222ddfae95496b5f17d0542db2` into base `76cb36661da9dba890c83e2130ff624f1ed29e90`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1140eed193f9f1e2669f0c3193134eb76d3c8a95 && git checkout 1140eed193f9f1e2669f0c3193134eb76d3c8a95
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 76cb36661da9dba890c83e2130ff624f1ed29e90 42d56e66cbcb04222ddfae95496b5f17d0542db2 && git checkout -B drift-repro 76cb36661da9dba890c83e2130ff624f1ed29e90 && git merge --no-ff 42d56e66cbcb04222ddfae95496b5f17d0542db2

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 76cb36661da9dba890c83e2130ff624f1ed29e90
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 76cb36661da9dba890c83e2130ff624f1ed29e90` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Scope — the paths `reviewFace` returns as `hits` on this PR's file list: packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.object-extension-place-and-cross-package-lists.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.related-lists-declared-is-tab-list.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts, docs/adr/0085-object-semantic-roles-over-surface-hint-blocks.md, docs/adr/0146-studio-designs-setup-administers-one-editor-per-item-paired-customize-package.md;
  plus every file IN THIS DIFF that directly implements or enforces them — the gate that enforces a rule, the code
  a jsdoc or schema line describes, the validator a skill teaches — reviewed for agreement with the contract.
  Widen it freely, ⛔ never below `hits`; the record's `Scope:` line names the implementing files apart from `hits`.
  The rest of the diff (tests, unrelated modules, lockfiles, generated output, changesets) is the lane seat's
  ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`, exactly as a standalone PR of those files.
  ④ judges the `hits` files and those implementing files ONLY:
  lockfiles, generated output, changesets and prose elsewhere in the PR are not reviewed;
  code outside the diff is READ to judge them, never reviewed.

Security — a `hits` path sits on the low-risk skills arm: when the change teaches security, auth or permission
  behaviour the path name doesn't show, the record says so and the seat adopting the record adds the `security` label.
  The record says so on its `Security-touching:` line, and the arm lands on `no` alone: write `no` ONLY when no changed
  hunk teaches permission, sharing, credential, token, authentication or other security behaviour, else `yes`.

⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs
   on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
   If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.
   Scratch space is `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/3d3cbaf6-4903-5fed-92d4-c2b94a45e868/scratchpad/pr-36236/` alone; nothing there you did not write this round is read.

Judge, in the record's own sections:
  ① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.
  ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.
  ③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated.
     On every face, SQL push-down: a new id materialisation or in-app join where SQL could push down is a
     finding unless a reason is given (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5: SQL first).
  ④ Design judgment — for EVERY `hits` file: does the change hold against the code it cites and the
     scenario it is accepted against? A skill file against the card's eval prompt and the spec it teaches
     on `main`; a schema file against the ruling or ADR it implements and its first consumer; an ADR
     against its first consumer and its execution plan. For EVERY implementing file in the diff: does the
     code agree with the contract, sentence by sentence? Read the cited code in the live tree, and try to
     break the design.
     Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit — a nit has no effect on correctness or the contract.
     A must-fix is a FAIL; a must-fix or should-fix earns a delta review of its fix; nits alone end the round.
     Spell a must-fix or should-fix with its id and grade, `S1 (should-fix) — …`, and a clean round as
     `No must-fix, no should-fix.`: the queue guard reads a graded finding as OPEN on this head and
     refuses the record; the delta record names those it closes by id alone, `S1: closed`.
     A nit is fixed only on the prose faces, or left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card: a fix
     anywhere else moves the head, and this record no longer covers it.
     ⛔ Judge the tree, never the PR body's account of it.
Sign `Implemented-by:` with the dev's branch and `Reviewed-by:` with your session id — the value is the FIRST

## 维护者速读
扩展包声明「我的字段、分组、子表排在原对象哪一项后面」这件事整体做对了，按你 02:36 的两条裁定：原对象声明了页签表或分组才生效，没声明就照旧并在启动日志里说明；别的包装上的子表不再被页签表藏起来，没写位置的排在页签末尾（审批、动态之前）。合并只在服务端做一次，记录页、表单和 Studio 看到同一个结果；Studio 保存时不会把扩展包的位置写进原对象。
有一个漏洞要补，改动很小：
① 卡上第 4 条规定扩展包不能挪动别人的东西。对「放一个子表页签」，服务端合并时会检查子表是不是这个包自己的，不是就跳过；但对「加一个分组、分组里放一张子表」，只有构建时检查，服务端合并时没有检查。这样一个不经正常构建的包，可以把原对象自己的子表搬进字段区，原来的页签也跟着消失。服务端合并要像页签那样检查并跳过。
L1 结论：补上这一处再审。

## 席位核对 — REWORK (L1-c) · repo:objectstack#1 · head `ce3ab59e` · 2026-11-22T04:26Z

**Card:** `Fixes #35901` (epic #35896). Rulings 7073014077 (F1 = F2 = (a)) and 7072511859 (the hiding this flips). Declarations: `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: semantic`, `Skills-docs: follow-up #35902`. Tier H (spec schema), 41 files, +2,552 / −50, so os-zhuang approves after the L2.

**Gates:**
- CI is 61 success · 9 expected skip on `ce3ab59e`, and mergeable is clean. `l1-face` is CLEAN.
- The branch is 8 behind `main`.
- The two fixes the seat relayed (the ADR-0122 aliases at `33961ec5`, and the migrate-meta cross-references by entry id at `ce3ab59e`) are not in the body yet. Add them before the hand-off.

### Must fix
1. **The merge does not skip a placed group whose `relatedList` names another owner's child.**
   - The PR body's small call 6 says item 4 ("an extension places only its own items") is enforced at parse, at `defineStack`, and by a skip plus warning in the merge. `applyExtensionPlacements` does that for list placements: `childPackageOf(childOf(list))`, owned by another package, is noted and skipped. It also does it for field placements (`ownFields`).
   - The group pass (pass 1) splices `{ ...entry.group }` as written. A group whose `relatedList` names the extended object's own child, or a third package's, is checked only by `collectExtensionPlacementErrors` at `defineStack`, which runs at `os build`, not when an installed artifact registers.
   - That group would move the owner's list into the field area. Under #35923's shipped rule, a group-placed table on a parent with a declared `relatedLists` that does not list it also loses its tab. This is the 「不能挪动或隐藏原对象和其他包的…页签」 the card forbids, reachable through the one placement shape the merge does not judge.
   - Fix: in pass 1, judge `entry.group.relatedList` (its string form, and its object form if `ObjectFieldGroupSchema` admits one) with the same `childPackageOf` verdict as pass 3. Skip and note a positive foreign verdict, and treat an unregistered child as no verdict. Pin it beside "foreign items skipped and named".
   - Group `fields` naming a foreign field is refused at parse (`refuseForeignPlacements`, `place[i].group.fields[j]`). If the registry can receive an unparsed body, the same skip there would complete the set. Say which in the reply.

### Read and found sound
- **`registry-extension-placement.ts`.**
  - The three passes run in `inPlacementOrder`: priority, then package id, then registration index.
  - In `splice`, an "after" item walks past earlier items placed after the same anchor, and a "before" item inserts at the anchor. Both give lowest priority first, as small call 1 says.
  - Missing anchors go to the end and are named. "Before" an unlisted trailing built-in is the end and is not named (small call 3).
  - The owner's position wins (`tabsArrange`, `listedSomewhere`, an existing group key), and that is what makes a re-fold idempotent.
  - A group without `fields` has its members read through `readFieldGroupMembership` and written out before the splice (small call 2).
  - Arm (a) is read in one place (`arrangementDeclared`), and the not-applied notes carry Fable's three points (`label` / `columns` inert, and `relatedListTitle` / `relatedListColumns` named).
  - When nothing applies, the body is returned by reference, so an object with no `place` is served unchanged.
- **The fold wiring.** `foldExtendersOntoDefinition` applies the placements after every contributor's fields are merged. `ownerGroupKeys` comes from the packaged owner, not a tenant base. `childPackageOf` uses the registry owner, and `null` means registered with no package. Notes are deduped per registry. `engine-registration.ts` carries `place`.
- **`defineStack`** (`collectExtensionPlacementErrors`). Per package body (ADR-0130 D4), a list or a group's `relatedList` must be a child this body defines with a lookup / master_detail field whose `reference` is the target, and a group key may not be the target's own. Anchors are left to lint, so removing an owner field never breaks a build (card acceptance 2).
- **Parse.** The three strict shapes, with aliases. A list placement refuses the built-in names. The refusals cover: both anchors at once, foreign fields (including a group's `fields`), an item placed twice, an item placed next to itself, and a field whose own `group` disagrees with its placement. The card's 「{ field: 'industry', group: 'other' }：校验拒绝」 is the foreign-field refusal.
- **Lint.** `extension-placement-not-applied` and `extension-placement-anchor-missing`, both warnings in the reference-integrity suite, each with an `os explain` entry, and saying they see only same-stack targets.
- **The console flip** (`deriveRelatedLists`). Another package's side list is kept on a declared parent only when both packages are known and differ (`sys_metadata` counts as no package), so package-less children keep #35897's hiding (small call 4). In `arrangeDeclaredTabs`, the unnamed related tabs rank `tail - 0.5`, just before a trailing run of listed approvals and stream tabs, which matches the server's `tabsEnd`. A group-placed (`isPrimary`) foreign table takes the body branch first, as before.
- **Studio.**
  - The buffer is the authored layer: `authoredObjectBuffer` gives `overlay ?? code`, never the served fold (`StudioDesignSurface.tsx` ~6245). So, as the body says, a save cannot copy a spliced extension entry into the owner.
  - The read-only "from <package>" row and the preview position match the page, and the test pins both, with a same-package control.
- **Migration** `object-extension-place-and-cross-package-lists`. It states the shipped-behaviour flip in its own text, the census, and that deployed metadata was not measured. Its printed text cites no issue id.

### Nits (do not block)
- `18.related-lists-declared-is-tab-list` now reads "…a child list another package adds included: it is hidden until the parent names it, … (no longer hidden since object-extension-place-and-cross-package-lists)". That is one clause asserting both. Rewrite it as history ("was hidden until the parent named it; since object-extension-place-and-cross-package-lists it shows at the end of the tabs"), or leave the merged entry's sentence and let the new entry carry the flip, as its own `reason` already does.
- `objectExtensionPlaceDescription` says "a group key the extended object **or another package** already declares … is refused (here, or at `defineStack` …)". `defineStack` judges the target's own keys only. Another package's same key is a merge note (`groupAddedBy`), not a refusal, so the sentence should say that.
- The migration's `replacement` ends "there is no way for the parent to hide it, short of `relatedList: false` on that package's FK". That FK is the other package's, so in practice the owner cannot hide it. That is the ruling's consequence; worth one sentence in the ADR-0085 note so the approver sees it.

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ce3ab59e98de9d671e866ee5158a3548c83898e1`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.object-extension-place-and-cross-package-lists.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.related-lists-declared-is-tab-list.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts, docs/adr/0085-object-semantic-roles-over-surface-hint-blocks.md, docs/adr/0146-studio-designs-setup-administers-one-editor-per-item-paired-customize-package.md + packages/objectql/src/registry-extension-placement.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry-object-registration.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-registration.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-extension-placement.ts, packages/lint/src/reference-integrity-suite.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/utils/deriveRelatedLists.ts, ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/synth/buildDefaultPageSchema.ts

Reviewed 2026-11-22T04:28Z on PR #36236 (card #35901), read-only: the net diff against `main` (merge base `48c732c4`), the card and its five comments, rulings 7073014077 and 7072511859, merged PR #35923, HotCRM `origin/main` at `5a17e454`, and the 70 check-runs on this head (all `success` or `skipped`, none failed). The rest of the diff (tests, Studio editor and vocabulary, i18n, generated spec artifacts, docs pages, the changeset) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`. Every finding below comes from reading the code; nothing was run.

### ① Derived judgments

- `ObjectExtensionSchema.place` is a new optional key: the accept set widens, and no body that parsed on `main` is refused. Right.
- Four new exported schemas (`ObjectExtensionFieldPlacementSchema`, `ObjectExtensionGroupPlacementSchema`, `ObjectExtensionListPlacementSchema`, `ObjectExtensionPlacementSchema`) and six types join the public surface, and the api-surface, authorable-surface, declaration-map, export-origins and JSON-schema baselines are regenerated in the diff. Right: `Build Core`, `Lint & Repo Gates` and `Spec property liveness` are green.
- The extension keys `fieldGroups` and `relatedLists` are still refused. `fieldGroups` only changes its prescription; `relatedLists` was already refused by the strict object as an unknown key and now carries a prescription. No accept-set change. Right.
- `defineStack` gains refusals (`collectExtensionPlacementErrors`) that only a `place` entry can reach, so no existing stack is newly refused. Right.
- `ObjectSchema.relatedLists` keeps its accept set and changes meaning: on a declared, non-empty list a side list whose child belongs to another package is no longer hidden. This is the flip ruling 7073014077 item 2 orders, and it is a semantic change, stated in the describe, the new migration entry and both ADR notes. Right.
- Two new `os validate` rules at warning severity, in the reference-integrity suite. They cannot fail a build that passed before. Right.
- `@objectstack/objectql`: the fold returns the merged body by reference when no extension carries `place` (`applyExtensionPlacements`, early return), so an app that writes no `place` is served as before. Right.
- HotCRM (first consumer): four extension files (o2c on `crm_contract`, `crm_account`, `crm_sales_order`; psa on `crm_expense`, `crm_expense_report`, `crm_expense_request`; revenue on `crm_sales_order`). None writes `place`, `fieldGroups` or `relatedLists`; their fields carry only a field-level `group`. No HotCRM object declares `relatedLists`, so the flip fires nowhere there. No declaration or object changes meaning. Right.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening)

The changeset declares the protocol kind `semantic` and takes `minor` on the six packages the diff moves (`@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@object-ui/app-shell`, `@object-ui/plugin-detail`, `@object-ui/i18n`). The diff publishes one added key and one changed meaning; `semantic` outranks `added`, nothing is narrowed, and a kind takes at least `minor`. The level matches. The PR body and the changeset carry the same two declaration lines, the ADR-0087 semantic entry is registered, and `Check Changeset` is green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Small calls 1, 2, 3, 5 and 7 of the PR body agree with the code and with the card's merge rules. Answered.
- Small call 4 (a child no package owns stays hidden until named) limits the ruled flip to the words of the ruling, "a child list another package adds". A child in the parent's paired `.custom` package has a different package id, so it shows. Answered; no escalation.
- Small call 6 (the own-items rule is held at parse, at `defineStack` and by the merge) does not hold in full: see S1 and S2.
- `PLACEMENT_ARRANGES_DECLARED_ONLY` is a compile-time constant set to the ruled arm, pinned by a test, not re-exported from the objectql index and not settable at runtime. The `false` arm is dead code. Answered.
- `open_questions`: the PR body carries none.
- SQL push-down: the change touches no query path. The fold reads registry maps in memory; it adds no id materialisation and no in-app join. No finding.
- For the maintainer and card #35902, a fact that differs from the follow-on line of ruling 7073014077: HotCRM objects do declare `fieldGroups` (30 object files, `crm_account`, `crm_contract` and `crm_expense` among them). A field or group placement would therefore apply in HotCRM as soon as a module writes one; only list placements wait for a parent to declare `relatedLists`. The ruling itself is unaffected. The changeset sentence "To use `place` on HotCRM's objects, the parent object first declares its `relatedLists`" is true of lists only.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`: the three shapes, the root refinement and the `place` describe implement card items 1 to 4 and both arms of ruling 7073014077. Anchors, the end position, the tie order and the declared-only arm match the merge sentence by sentence, except where the findings below say otherwise.

`packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts`: `collectExtensionPlacementErrors` judges a list and a placed group's `relatedList` per package body, and a group key against the target's own keys. It runs before the early return for a stack with no objects. It holds against the HotCRM module shape (objects and `objectExtensions` in one body).

Both migration entries: the new entry states the flip, the unchanged cases and the census; I confirmed the HotCRM half of the census. The one-clause edit to the #35897 entry points at the new entry. Hold.

ADR-0085 note and ADR-0146 D10 note: add-only, dated, and they agree with the ruling. The D10 sentence "refused at parse or at `defineStack` and skipped by the merge with a warning" is wider than the code in two places (S1, S2).

Implementing files: the fold wiring, the manifest loop, the once-per-registry notes, `deriveRelatedLists` and `arrangeDeclaredTabs` agree with the contract. The merge and the browser compute the same end of the tabs.

Findings:

The `place` describe, the `refuseForeignPlacements` docstring ("the registry merge for every door") and the ADR-0146 note all say the merge skips such an item with a warning. - S2 (should-fix) — an extension can move a field the owner declares. Parse and merge both read "own" as a key of the extension's `fields` (`isOwn`, `placementContributorsOf` building `ownFields` from `Object.keys(body.fields)`). ADR-0146 D10 admits an extension that redeclares an owner field with display-only changes (`judgeRedeclaredOwnerFields`; a boot only warns). Fix: a placed field must also not be a field the owner declares (skip and name it in the merge; refuse it where the owner is known), and add the test.

The lint rule accepts any anchor that some extension of the target places (`placedLists`, `placedGroups`, `placedFields`). The merge finds an anchor only if it is already spliced: passes run in priority, package id and entry order. With `place: [{ list: 'a', after: 'b' }, { list: 'b' }]`, or a lower-priority package anchoring on a higher-priority one's item, the merge sends the item to the end and names it in the boot log, and `os validate` is silent. Neither `collectExtensionPlacementErrors`, `validate-extension-placement.ts` nor `validate-related-list-refs.ts` reads a placement's `columns`, so an unknown column reaches the served `relatedLists`. The child is in the extension's own package, so the build can always judge it. Fix: give a placement's columns the same check.
- N1 (nit) — the `place` describe says a group key "the extended object or another package already declares" is refused. Another package's key is only skipped by the merge with a note; nothing refuses it. Reword when the head moves for the fixes above.
